I would keep my land mainly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that fits Quzhou County best and it is the way I would reduce risk while keeping grain income steady. At the start of the growing season, I would first focus on finishing the winter wheat already in the field, then follow it with summer maize after harvest. I would choose improved or hybrid seed, not traditional seed, because I would want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and more reliable yield. For wheat, I would use moderate fertilizer, give a few irrigations at key stages, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed for aphids, rust, or other common problems. After wheat harvest, I would quickly prepare the land and sow summer maize to catch the season on time. For maize, I would use a bit more nitrogen, fewer irrigations than wheat if rainfall is normal, and control weeds and insects with a small number of pesticide applications. For tillage, I would mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical, fast, and suits my conditions. I would not spread risk across many small crops; I would rather plant the crops I know well, can manage with my labor, and can sell easily.
